key_concept: Gymnosperms are heterosporous seed plants whose gametophytes are reduced and stay within the sporangia, and whose ovules, and hence seeds, are naked (not enclosed in an ovary or fruit wall).
steps: Statement I: In gymnosperms, the male gametophyte (pollen grain) develops inside the microsporangium. The female gametophyte develops inside the megasporangium (nucellus) of the ovule. Neither has an independent free-living existence, so Statement I is correct.
Note: The pollen grain is later released and carried to the ovule. It still never lives independently like the gametophytes of bryophytes or pteridophytes.
Statement II: The word 'gymnosperm' means naked seed. The ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, before or after fertilisation. So the seeds that develop are exposed, and Statement II is correct.
Both statements are correct, which matches option (1).
final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
why_not_others: Options (3) and (4) come from doubting one statement. Students may think the release of pollen contradicts Statement I, or confuse the seed coat with an ovary wall in Statement II. Option (2) fails because both statements are core features of gymnosperms.
common_trap: Thinking 'seeds not covered' means gymnosperm seeds have no seed coat, when it actually means the seed is not enclosed within an ovary or fruit.
time_saving_tip: Recall the defining line on gymnosperms: the reduced male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence and remain within the sporangia, and the ovules are naked. Both statements come straight from this.
